account:
Today I have kept my morning office work, market walk, and lunch appointment, and I am now at town hall for the thirteen hundred accounts. My appointment book also lists tea at fifteen hundred and an office engagement at sixteen thirty. The neighbour personally confirmed tea at the cottage at x sixteen, z one hundred and five, just east of the ferry. I have passed that address to the secretary.

The most unusual report is that the builder called for the innkeeper near the inn this morning and asked to meet privately. Several townsfolk repeated the same words, so these may all be retellings of one shout rather than separate evidence. I also heard the builder shouting later, but could not make out the words. I do not know whether the private meeting happened or what it concerned. It could simply concern ordinary building or inn business; I have no evidence of wrongdoing or of a plan involving me.

Townsfolk have reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and, later, a sack of bread near the plaza. That sounds consistent with baking and selling bread, although I have not personally checked the business. The secretary handled the appointment book this morning and offered to verify the tea details. Nothing I have read establishes that the appointments were altered. The innkeeper, freight, and secretary are presently around town hall, but their presence alone does not establish a connection. I heard recent speech without understanding it and cannot draw conclusions from it.

I still have a feeling that town business may be happening without my knowledge, but the purpose of the builder's requested private conversation remains unknown. I should attend to the accounts, keep the confirmed tea appointment, and ask ordinary, discreet questions rather than assume a conspiracy.
